subject: STUDENT-FACING: the AI assistant is briefed on content nobody can click. Cross-referenced the 272 evidence-backed unreachable catalog entries against all 14 _app/bot-knowledge-*.html files (the pages that tell the assistant what exists): 31 are described to the bot, and ~25 of those are the ENTIRE ai house cluster. Verified the ai cluster is genuinely unreachable rather than runtime-rendered: checked all 8 ai sub-hubs live (/houses/ai + agents, advanced, hubs, modules, automation, cli-tools, azure-openai) -- 44/10/11/4/8/8/8/9 anchors respectively, ZERO links to ai-prompt-injection.lab.html on any of them, and the only file under houses/ai containing that name is the lab itself. So a student who asks the assistant for the Prompt Injection Attack and Defense Lab gets told it exists and cannot reach it. Worse than an unreachable catalog entry, because the platform actively recommends it. Affects ai (~25), plus eye and script (1 each confirmed). DECISION NEEDED per cluster, same as #272: wire up or retire -- and if retiring, the bot-knowledge entry must go too or the bot keeps recommending it.
description:
Measured 2026-07-31
[2026-08-01 02:00] SCOPED PRECISELY 2026-07-31. Checked whether the assistant is briefed on files that do not EXIST (worse than unreachable): it is not. The 14 bot-knowledge files reference 276 distinct .html filenames and every real one is present in _app. My first pass reported 6 'missing' -- all six were artifacts of a loose regex matching SUFFIX FRAGMENTS out of longer names (applet.html and tool.html from '*.applet.html'/'*.tool.html', combined.html from 'bot-knowledge-combined.html') plus two literal placeholders (NN.lab.html, NN.quiz.html in bot-knowledge-matrix.html, where NN stands for a number). No action needed on existence.
So the defect is purely REACHABILITY: 31 briefed files exist and serve, but nothing links them. That is the cleaner and more actionable framing -- the fix is to wire them up or retire both the content and its bot-knowledge entry together, not to chase dead references.
